activities.title: A Day in the Life of a Baker
activities.instruction: Listen carefully! 🎧 Clear your ears and to a baker talk about his job, then answer the questions.

questions.question: Where does Ahmed work?

options.text: No, but he wears a clean apron and a hat.

content.transcript: My name is Ahmed, and I'm a baker. My job is hard work, but I like it. I don't work in an office or a hospital. I work in a small bakery. I have to start work very early, at 4 o'clock in the morning, while everyone is sleeping. I make bread, cakes, and pastries. I don't wear a uniform, but I always wear a clean white apron and a hat. I meet lots of nice people when they come to buy fresh bread for their breakfast.

sentences.text: A secretary ___ at a desk in an office.

blanks.hint: Use a verb from the reading text. Remember the third person '-s'.

sentences.explanation: We add '-s' to the verb for he/she/it in the present simple. A secretary is a 'he' or 'she'.

sentences.text: A policeman ___ a uniform.

blanks.hint: What do you do with clothes?

activities.title: Making Negative Sentences
activities.instruction: Reading time! 📖 Read carefully and the positive sentence and rewrite it as a negative sentence. Remember to use 'don't' or 'doesn't'.
activities.compensates: This is a digital, self-correcting version of Workbook activity F.

sentences.explanation: For a singular noun (a secretary), we use 'does not' or 'doesn't' before the base form of the verb (work).
For a plural noun (policemen), we use 'do not' or 'don't' before the base form of the verb (work).
sentences.correct_transformed: Policemen don't work in a clinic.

sentences.explanation: The text says 'I don't have to wear a uniform'. For 'a dentist', we use 'doesn't have to'.
sentences.correct_transformed: A dentist doesn't have to wear a uniform.

sentences.original: We go to school on Fridays.
sentences.explanation: For the pronoun 'We', we use 'do not' or 'don't' to make the sentence negative.
sentences.correct_transformed: We don't go to school on Fridays.

sentences.original: My father goes to work on Fridays.
sentences.explanation: For a singular subject (My father), we use 'doesn't' and the base form of the verb (go).
sentences.correct_transformed: My father doesn't go to work on Fridays.

activities.title: Listening: Holiday Conversations
activities.instruction: Listen carefully! 🎧 Clear your ears and to three short conversations about the holidays. Then, answer the questions.
activities.compensates: Teacher-led activity 'Listen for specific information' (PB3, CS2).

options.text: He went to a village by the sea.

questions.question: In Conversation 1, where did the boy go?
What did the boy in Conversation 1 do?
Did the girl in Conversation 2 go away?

options.text: She went to a football match.

questions.question: Which activity did the girl in Conversation 3 NOT do?

content.transcript: Conversation 1. Boy 1: Did you go away in the holidays? Boy 2: Yes, I went to a village by the sea. Boy 1: What did you do there? Boy 2: Oh, I went swimming every day. And fishing. It was great! Conversation 2. Girl 1: Did you go away in the holidays? Girl 2: No, I stayed at home. Girl 1: What did you do all the time? Girl 2: Oh, lots of things. I saw my friends every day. We went shopping. I made some clothes. Conversation 3. Girl 1: Did you go away in the holidays? Girl 3: No, I stayed at home. Girl 1: What did you do all the time? Girl 3: Not very much. I got up late every day. And I read lots of books. Oh, and I learned to cook.
